findings.title: Slots on a date-override day skip the busy-time check, allowing double bookings
findings.body:
When a date override matches the slot's day and the slot is not rejected by it, `checkIfIsAvailable` hits `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` and returns before `busy.every(...)` runs.

Busy times (existing Cal bookings and external calendar events) are only checked in this function. So on any day with a date override, a host's bookings and calendar conflicts are ignored and already-booked slots are offered again.

This is not limited to round-robin. Personal event types also go through the `fixedHosts.every(...)` path, because `isFixed` is true when there is no `schedulingType`. Every user with a date override can be double-booked on that day.

The override check should only reject slots; the busy check must still run afterwards.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects a slot if it falls outside ANY range for that weekday
findings.body:
`workingHours.find(...)` returns a match as soon as one working-hour entry for the slot's weekday does not contain the slot, and the slot is then marked unavailable. A slot should only be rejected if it is outside all ranges for that day.

This breaks two common cases:
- Users with split hours on the same day (e.g. 9–12 and 13–17). A 10:00 slot is outside 13–17, so it is rejected.
- Users whose local hours cross UTC midnight. `getWorkingHours` splits these into two entries with overlapping day sets. For Mon–Fri 9–17 in America/Los_Angeles you get `{days:[1..5], 960–1439}` and `{days:[2..6], 0–0}`. Every Tue–Fri slot is then outside the second entry and rejected.

This runs for every fixed host, including the single host of every personal event type. Most users in US timezones would lose most of their availability. The check should test that the slot is inside some range for that day (or be removed, since `getSlots` already generates slots only within working hours).

findings.title: Working-hours 'end' is computed from the slot start instead of the slot end
findings.body:
`const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to `start`. As a result, `end > workingHour.endTime` never catches slots that start inside working hours but run past the end.

It should be derived from `slotEndTime`. Midnight wrap-around also needs handling: slotEndTime may fall on the next UTC day, where hour*60+minute is small.

findings.title: Override end check uses slot start, so slots extending past the override end are accepted
findings.body:
The slot is only rejected when `slotStartTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`.

With an override ending at 18:00 and a 60-minute event:
- a 17:30 slot (ending 18:30) passes;
- an 18:00 slot also passes, because `isAfter` is false when the times are equal.

The point of this change is to enforce a fixed host's override in round-robin events, so slots that end after the override end should be rejected. Compare `slotEndTime` against the override end instead (`isAfter`).

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with ===, so the 'unavailable all day' branch never fires
findings.body:
`dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two freshly created object references and is always false. The intended detection of a zero-length ("unavailable") override never triggers.

The later checks do not fully cover it. A slot starting exactly at the override instant is neither before start nor after end. It sets `dateOverrideExist = true` and is returned as available, which also bypasses the busy check.

Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `valueOf()` instead.

findings.title: Override day matching uses server-local formatting and UTC calendar days instead of the organizer's local day
findings.body:
There are two problems with how the override's day is matched to the slot.

First, the format calls disagree on timezone. `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` formats in the server process's local timezone, while `slotStartTime` is `.utc()`. On a server not running in UTC, the dates can mismatch.

Second, even on UTC servers the logic compares the UTC calendar date of the real override start with the UTC date of the slot. An organizer's local override day usually spans two UTC dates. For a PST organizer with an override on day D:
- slots on UTC date D that belong to local day D-1 (evening hours) are treated as part of the override day and wrongly rejected;
- override slots that fall on UTC date D+1 are not recognized as override slots and fall through to the working-hours check.

Matching should be done on the organizer-local date of the slot (e.g. `slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone)`) against the override's date.

findings.title: Converted override wraps around midnight and is dropped, leaving the day with no slots
findings.body:
The override is shifted into the invitee timezone and reduced to `hour()*60+minute()`, which wraps modulo a day.

If the shifted range crosses invitee midnight, startTime > endTime. For example, an IST 14:00–18:00 override seen from Pacific/Auckland becomes 21:30–01:30. A shifted end of exactly midnight becomes 0.

`buildSlots` skips ranges with `start >= end`. Because the user's working hours for that day were already spliced out in favor of the override, the invitee sees no slots at all that day, and the portion on the next invitee day is never produced.

The override needs to be split across invitee days, or the end clamped to 1440, rather than computed modulo 24h.

findings.title: Missing override timeZone silently falls back to the runtime's local timezone
findings.body:
`TimeRange.timeZone` is declared optional. When it is absent, `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` gets `undefined` and the dayjs tz plugin uses the default/system local timezone.

In that case the organizer offset is computed against the client or server machine's timezone instead of the organizer's, and override slots are shifted incorrectly without any error. Any caller of `getSlots` that does not attach `timeZone` gets wrong results.

Fall back explicitly to `organizerTimeZone`, which is already a parameter, or make the field required.

findings.title: No tests for the main fix or for the new availability checks' edge cases
